rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and Methods / Results <U+2014> laboratory anticlogging test of 10 cycles over 10 weeks with muddy water with and without 2% urea, measuring emitter discharge, dry weight of clogging materials, microorganism counts, XRD/FE-SEM and urea adsorption kinetics.
rows.notes: The study is a laboratory emitter-clogging experiment with no crop, no field plots and no measurement of yield, crop quality or nutrient uptake. It reports discharge reduction rate, uniformity coefficient, clogging-material composition and microbial counts under urea fertigation with muddy water. It provides no own evidence that advanced/drip irrigation increases crop yield, optimizes quality or reduces excessive nutrient consumption relative to conventional drip. The review may have intended a different Liu et al. 2019 paper.

rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and Methods / Results <U+2014> own laboratory anticlogging experiment (10 weekly cycles, muddy water with and without 2% urea) measuring emitter discharge, clogging-material dry weight and microorganism numbers.
rows.notes: The study contains nothing on pesticides or pest control. It only reports emitter clogging behaviour (Drr, Cu, dry weight, mineral composition, bacteria/fungi/actinomycete counts in lateral sediments) under urea muddy-water fertigation. The microbial counts refer to clogging organisms inside laterals, not crop pests. No own evidence that drip reduces pesticide applications.
